jobs.description:

Executive Summary

Contra Costa Health (CCH) is seeking an exceptional executive leader to serve as its inaugural Chief Operating Officer (COO), a newly created position designed to modernize one of California's largest and most comprehensive integrated public health systems.

The COO will help shape the future of a healthcare system that uniquely combines a health plan, a public hospital, community health centers, behavioral health services, public health, housing and homelessness services, and community health and safety programs under one integrated organization.

As the County's primary Medi-Cal provider, Contra Costa Health touches the lives of a significant portion of the County's 1.2M residents. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to improve access, quality, efficiency, and health outcomes for some of California's most vulnerable populations while helping lead the organization through one of the most transformational periods in its history.

About Contra Costa Health

Contra Costa Health is one of the most comprehensive county health systems in the United States.
Serving one of the Country’s largest and most diverse counties, the department integrates:
Contra Costa Regional Medical Center and Health Centers - A county-operated public hospital and network of nine primary care health centers
Contra Costa Health Plan
Behavioral Health Services
Public Health
Health, Housing and Homelessness
Community Health and Safety

Together these services create an integrated delivery system that allows Contra Costa Health to influence both how care is delivered and how it is financed—an uncommon model that enables innovation, flexibility, and system-wide coordination.
The department oversees approximately 5,000 employees and operates with an annual budget approaching $4B.

To learn more about Contra Costa Health, check out their website: cchealth.org

The Position

Reporting directly to the Director of Health Services, the Chief Operating Officer serves as a key member of the department’s executive team and works collaboratively to develop strategy, align resources, and enhance organizational effectiveness across Contra Costa Health.
Leading operational strategy and providing direct oversight for major divisions in Contra Costa Health, including Contra Costa Regional Medical Center, affiliated Health Centers, Contra Costa Health Plan, Behavioral Health, and Community Health and Safety divisions such as Public Health and Health, Housing and Homelessness.

Primary responsibilities include:
Serves as the Director of Health Services’ designee in their absence, ensuring continuity of executive leadership, decision-making, and operational performance
Plans, develops, and implements long-term system objectives, including modernization initiatives, service expansion, and strategies to support sustainable organizational growth
Oversee department-wide operations to improve transparency, reduce duplication, increase efficiency, and implement consistent standards and best practices across the organization
Develops and maintains collaborative working relationships with other County departments to strengthen coordination, promote innovation, and optimize service delivery
Leads the adaptation of organizational systems and operations to effectively respond to evolving healthcare delivery models, financing structures, and managed care environments
Collaborates with the CCH Chief Financial Officer in the financial management of CCH, including long-term budget planning and alignment of operational and fiscal strategy
Provides oversight to Deputy Directors across all CCH divisions, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and performance standards
Oversee executive responses to regulatory and inspection findings, ensuring compliance, accountability, and continuous improvement across the health system

The Ideal Candidate

Contra Costa Health seeks an accomplished executive with operational expertise, leadership presence, and strategic mindset to lead a highly complex public healthcare organization through transformational change.

The successful candidate will bring:

Executive Healthcare Operations Experience

Extensive executive leadership within large, complex healthcare organizations
Experience overseeing operations for hospitals, integrated delivery systems, health systems, or large ambulatory networks
Demonstrated success leading largescale and complex operational transformation and performance improvement
Experience aligning clinical operations with financial sustainability
Experience working in a unionized environment

Strategic Leadership

The ideal candidate will possess:
Strong operational leadership expertise
Excellent relationship-building skills
Political awareness and sound judgment
Data-driven decision making
Commitment to accountability and continuous improvement

Minimum Qualifications:

Education:
Possession of a master’s degree from an accredited college or university in public health, hospital or healthcare administration, business or public administration, social or behavioral sciences, health sciences, social work, or a closely related field.

Experience:
Seven (7) years of full-time (or equivalent) progressively responsible professional management experience within a healthcare or human services organization. This experience must include at least three (3) years in an executive-level leadership role within a large, complex, and diverse public or nonprofit organization providing health or human services.

Candidates are encouraged to express interest early in the recruitment process. This position will remain open until filled. For first consideration, please submit your application by September 7th, 2026.

Applications should be submitted through Contra Costa County.

jobs.title: Associate Director of Development and Alumni Relations
jobs.description:
Reporting to the Associate Vice President for University Advancement (AVP), the Associate Director of Development and Alumni Relations is responsible for annual giving, scholarship stewardship, and alumni relations for MBKU and all three programs (Southern California College of Optometry, School of Physician Assistant Studies, and the College of Pharmacy). This position is responsible for annual fundraising from individuals and organizations at the $24,999 level and below, through annual giving appeals and individual portfolio outreach. The Associate Director works closely with the AVP for University Advancement to develop fundraising priorities and execute annual fundraising plans for MBKU and the three programs. This position actively manages a prospect portfolio of 75-125 individuals, identifies and qualifies new prospects, and oversees the annual solicitations and stewardship for scholarship donors. Additionally, the Associate Director works closely with the Alumni Council and affiliated program-based alumni societies and the AVP, to develop programs to engage alumni and build relationships to secure private support and build alumni pride.

Essential Duties And Responsi­­bilities

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Articulate the case for support with effectiveness; communicate the priorities, goals and mission of the university.
Articulate the value of gifts to MBKU and the three programs to meet programmatic fundraising priorities and goals.
Manage and actively engage a portfolio of approximately 75-125 alumni and organizational prospects. Conduct strategic outreach to identify, qualify, cultivate, solicit and steward donors.
Develop and execute individualized cultivation, solicitation and stewardship strategies designed to advance prospects through the major gift pipeline. Performance expectations include consistently achieving monthly, quarterly, and annual metrics including but not limited to outreach attempts, number of meaningful donor visits, substantive donor conversations, gift solicitations, and other key metrics as defined by UA leadership.
Develop proposals and other necessary written collateral to secure private support for annual campus and program priorities including scholarships, sponsorships, programmatic needs and other college based and MBKU programmatic fundraising priorities.
Write, develop, and manage the execution of annual giving appeals.
Responsible for developing increasing levels of involvement and support among donors and prospects utilizing best practices for cultivation and stewardship through regular correspondence and contacts in person, by phone, mail and email.
Assist with annual giving, scholarship, Alumni Council and Club engagement activities and events. Assist the AVP in developing programs to increase engagement activities for alumni, including alumni awards programming, regional receptions, alumni giving clubs and other volunteer opportunities that align with institutional and program-based priorities.
Contribute to the overall strategic plan for the office of University Advancement as it relates to Alumni Relations, scholarship fundraising, stewardship of donors, and annual fund outreach.
Assist with Alumni Council meetings by preparing agendas, scheduling meetings and working with the AVP to record minutes and provide other resources needed.
Participate in professional conference alumni receptions and programs.
Field phone calls and inquiries from alumni and donors and assist or direct them to the proper UA representative.
Utilize the Raiser’s Edge database to record donor interactions, solicitations, opportunities, and other significant fundraising/stewardship information and actions on behalf of MBKU, complying with expectations as outlined for UA Prospect Management.
Collect data and generate reports for assigned prospects as well as the scholarship and annual fund programs as needed.
Engage in campus and community activities and functions as assigned.
In collaboration with the UA team, develop donor stewardship reports for assigned prospects and scholarship donors
Be an active and collaborative team member in University Advancement and with colleagues across the campus to accomplish goals.

Qualification Requirements

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each duty satisfactorily. The r­equirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

2-5 years of annual fundraising experience, preferably at a higher education institution; or equivalent combination of education/experience.
Thorough working knowledge of annual fundraising, donor relations, alumni relations concepts, principles, procedures, and techniques.
Direct solicitation fundraising experience both orally and in written format.
Strong knowledge of applicable laws, rules, regulations, policies, etc.
Strong organizational, analytical and critical thinking skills, including skills in creative and effective decision-making and problem identification / avoidance / resolution, and project management skills.
Strong skills in maintaining confidentiality.
Ability to work independently with department, school and institutional goals in mind.
Team-oriented strategist able to effectively manage complex situations involving multiple and sometimes competing constituencies.
Skill in communicating persuasively, both orally and in writing, about private philanthropy in general and in particular as it applies to MBKU.

Preferred:

Thorough working knowledge of the location, its vision, mission, goals, objectives, achievements and infrastructure. Working knowledge of Raiser’s Edge or comparable a donor/prospect database system.

Understanding of academic and education functions and operating principals of a university.
Computer literate in Microsoft Office, Excel, Raiser’s Edge or similar donor databases.
Excellent interpersonal skills.
Excellent written, verbal and non-verbal communication skills.
Willingness to work weekends and evenings as needed.
Excellent organizational skills with the ability to prioritize daily based on demands and deadlines.

Required:

EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training at a similar institution or non-profit.
2+ years of experience in fundraising, donor relations, annual fundraising and/or alumni relations and fundraising.
Strong writing skills with experience developing annual fund solicitations, gift agreements and stewardship reports.
2+ years of event planning experience.
Demonstrated experience working with campus partners and volunteers.
Demonstrated organizational skills to achieve timely progress on multiple simultaneous complex projects, meet deadlines and maintain a high level of productivity.

Preferred:

Working knowledge of the higher education and/or health care environment.

About The University

SEE YOURSELF HERE

Located on a beautiful, seven-acre campus in Fullerton, California, MBKU is an independent, private, non-profit, accredited educational institution. MBKU is home to the Southern California College of Optometry, the School of PA Studies, College of Pharmacy and the Doctor of Medical Science Program (DMSc) . MBKU owns and operates three health care centers at their clinical teaching facility, Ketchum Health, providing a vision center and PA medical clinic practice in Orange County and second vision center in Los Angeles.

A TRADITION OF EXCELLENCE SINCE 1904

In 1904, Marshall B. Ketchum, MD, opened the Los Angeles School of Ophthalmology and Optometry in Los Angeles. Dr. Ketchum was a visionary entrepreneur and prominent leader in the optometric profession. He made very significant and long-standing contributions in his field of care, in California and throughout the nation.

In the early ‘70s the College moved to its current home in Fullerton, CA and was renamed Southern California College of Optometry. But even the pioneering Dr. Ketchum could not have envisioned his school would grow to become Marshall B. Ketchum University, an independent, private, non-profit, accredited educational institution encompassing multiple disciplines.

BE AT THE FOREFRONT OF HEALTH CARE EDUCATION

Marshall B. Ketchum University offers career opportunities that will put you at the forefront of health care education. You will be provided with learning and advancement opportunities, as well as a culture that recognizes the importance of fun, employee appreciation and a work-life balance.

Our mission is to educate caring, inspired health care professionals who are prepared to deliver collaborative, patient-centric health care in an interprofessional environment. By joining our family, you can help us reimagine the future and inspire future health care leaders.

INTERPROFESSIONAL HEALTH CARE LEADERS

At Marshall B. Ketchum University, we have led the way in interprofessional healthcare, building on a century of experience as an optometry school. In 2012, the first Physician Assistant program in Orange County was added, followed by the College of Pharmacy program in 2014. Most recently in 2024, we expanded our offerings with the addition of the fully-online Doctor of Medical Science(DMSc) program. Side-by-side in group discussions, community service, and clinical experience, our OD, PA, PharmD and DMSc students learn what it means to deliver patient-centered health care as a collaborative team of professionals.

BENEFITS

MBKU provides an excellent benefits package including medical, dental, and life insurance, free vision exams, short and long term disability, generous paid time off plans, a university-sponsored retirement plan. See our website under Employment for more details regarding benefits of working for MBKU (www.ketchum.edu).

MBKU is an equal opportunity employer; requirements are subject to possible modification to reasonably accommodate individuals with disabilities.

NON-DISCRIMINATION STATEMENT

MBKU is committed to providing an environment in which all individuals are treated with respect and professionalism. In accordance with applicable federal and state laws, it is University policy to prevent the unlawful discrimination against students, applicants for admission, employees, applicants for employment and patients requesting treatment on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, disability, age or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. The University also prohibits sexual harassment and harassment on any of the above bases (please refer to the Title IX page for more information).

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead LucentAI, an AI-native litigation operations venture in build at FutureSight. This offers meaningful founder equity, not a salary.

LucentAI serves as an autopilot for medical-records and discovery operations in small-to-mid insurance-defence firms. Embedding in case-management systems, it retrieves and reviews records, flags key facts with confidence links, checks billing reasonableness, and chronologically triages discovery. This human-gated system excludes legal drafting, externalizing review capacity so firms can scale case volume without adding headcount.

Market validation through FutureSight's discovery interviews confirmed strong demand:

Operations is the wedge; autopilot is the vision. All buyers wanted managed operations. LucentAI provides end-to-end automation, earning trust incrementally by handling routine work silently while keeping legal drafting human

Market Context

We target underserved small-to-mid US insurance-defence firms.

The Phase-1 beachhead SAM is $150M-$600M across 1,500-3,000 firms; the full roadmap reaches a ≥$100M obtainable market (SOM ≈ $110M-$360M).

About MyFriendBen
MyFriendBen is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit dedicated to making it easy for people to understand and access the government benefits, tax credits, and nonprofit programs they're eligible for. Our free, anonymous online screening tool checks eligibility for 40+ programs in minutes and estimates their dollar value — with no cost to use and a promise never to sell user data.

Originally incubated at Gary Community Ventures in Colorado, MyFriendBen is now an independent nonprofit with its national hub based in Denver and is expanding into additional states. To date, MyFriendBen has connected more than 140,000 households to benefits, for an estimated $85 million in impact, with families identifying an average of $2,500 per month in benefits and tax credits.

As MyFriendBen scales nationally, our donors and funders — foundations, corporations, government grantors, and individuals who believe in equitable access to the safety net — are essential partners in that growth, as is the internal team and culture that supports it.

Position Summary
The Director  of Operations is responsible for building and running the internal backbone of MyFriendBen — fundraising and grants, people operations, hiring and onboarding, team alignment, culture, and day-to-day organizational operations — so the organization can scale nationally without losing what makes it work. This role owns the systems, relationships, and practices that keep a fast-growing, distributed team funded, connected, effective, and aligned around MyFriendBen's mission.

The VP will manage a growing portfolio of fundraising and grant relationships — including grant writing, grant management, and donor stewardship — while also owning full-cycle hiring and onboarding, HR policies and practices, and team culture across a remote, multi-state staff. The role also oversees core operational functions, including finance and budget administration, vendor and systems management, and organizational planning, in partnership with the Executive Director.

This role works closely with the Executive Director, program, and leadership team, and reports regularly to the board of directors on fundraising results and organizational health. The ideal candidate brings progressive fundraising and operations experience, an entrepreneurial mindset, and genuine enthusiasm for MyFriendBen's mission of expanding access to public benefits.

This is a remote position with a preference for candidates based in or near Denver, CO, who can work periodically from MyFriendBen's Denver hub as needed.

Essential Functions and Responsibilities

Fundraising & Grants

Manage a growing portfolio of foundation, corporate, and government funders
, guiding each through the full gift and grant cycle — identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
Research, write, and submit grant proposals and letters of inquiry
that are compelling, accurate, and aligned with MyFriendBen's mission, data, and strategic priorities.
Own grant management end-to-end
, including tracking deliverables, budgets, and deadlines, and preparing timely, accurate reports for foundation and government funders.
Build authentic, trust-based relationships with donors, board members, and funding partners
, including drafting appeals, impact reports, and donor communications.
Maintain the fundraising and grants pipeline in MyFriendBen's donor database/CRM
, and report revenue projections and progress toward goals to leadership and the board.
Represent MyFriendBen at funder convenings, conferences, and donor events
, and stay current on philanthropic trends and the public-benefits/anti-poverty funding landscape.

Own full-cycle hiring
— job postings, sourcing, interview coordination, and offer management — in partnership with hiring managers across the organization.
Design and run onboarding
so new hires ramp quickly, understand MyFriendBen's mission and systems, and feel connected to the team from day one.
Build and maintain HR infrastructure
, including policies, employee handbook, benefits administration, and compliance across the states where MyFriendBen has staff.
Own team culture as a core priority
, leading practices — all-hands meetings, team rituals, feedback loops, recognition programs, and retreats — that keep a remote, distributed staff connected, engaged, and aligned as the organization scales.
Champion transparency, trust, and shared purpose
, using regular staff surveys and check-ins to monitor morale and strengthen retention.
Support performance management
, including goal-setting, check-ins, and professional development planning for staff.
Serve as a trusted resource
for staff on people-related questions, and help resolve team or interpersonal issues as they arise.

Operations & Organizational Effectiveness

Oversee day-to-day organizational operations
, including budget administration, contracts, vendor management, and internal systems (HRIS, project management, communication tools).
Partner with the Executive Director
on annual operating plans, budget projections, and organizational strategy, including fundraising and grant revenue targets.
Develop and maintain internal policies and processes
that support a growing, multi-state team, ensuring consistency, compliance, and efficiency.
Regularly report on organizational health
— fundraising results, staffing, budget, and operational metrics — to leadership and the board of directors.
Manage relationships with outside vendors
(payroll, benefits, HR/legal counsel, IT) and evaluate new tools or partners as needs evolve.
Identify and implement improvements
to internal operations as MyFriendBen expands into new states.
Perform other related duties as assigned.

Working knowledge of HR practices, employment law fundamentals, and people operations across multiple states.
Experience building or scaling hiring, onboarding, and culture programs at a growing organization.
Strong understanding of nonprofit operations, including budgeting, compliance, and vendor management.
Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to craft persuasive proposals and handle sensitive personnel matters with equal skill.

Passion for MyFriendBen's mission of expanding equitable, dignified access to public benefits.

The Colorado LiftED Foundation is a long-term partner to youth and families in the Denver metro area, offering academic, social, and emotional support so no one has to navigate school and life alone. Since our founding in 1988, we've leveraged proven methods to give youth equal access to the resources they need to succeed — working toward a Colorado where every young person has equal access to educational and career opportunities that ignite their innate potential.

About the Position

The Director of Development & Engagement owns CLF's individual-giving engine — donor relationships, signature events, and year-round giving campaigns that turn community belief into sustained support for youth. Reporting to the Senior Director of Development, the Director sets and executes the strategy for donor cultivation and stewardship, the Annual Gala and signature events, and CLF's giving campaigns (Colorado Gives Day, End-of-Year Giving, and beyond), and owns the revenue those efforts produce.

This is a builder's role with a growth path: in year one it is non-supervisory, with the Director carrying strategy and donor relationships directly, supported by a contracted event coordinator and volunteers, and partnering closely with the CEO, Senior Director of Development, and Development Operations & Communications Manager. The ideal candidate is a strategic relationship-builder who is equally comfortable shaping a multi-year donor plan, running a flawless gala, and reading a campaign dashboard to course-correct mid-stream — someone who treats each donor as a long-term partner whose commitment is meant to outlast any single gift.

This Role Lives All Five CLF Values

A Seat at the Table —
Donor and volunteer experiences authentically include the voices of youth, families, and community.
An Inch Wide, A Mile Deep —
A focused, high-quality donor portfolio beats chasing volume.
Once a Dreamer, Always a Dreamer —
Every donor and volunteer is stewarded with the same long-term commitment CLF brings to youth.
Whatever It Takes —
Relentless, creative follow-through on cultivation, events, and campaigns alike.
We Not Me —
Individual giving is shared organizational infrastructure, not a department off to one side.

Key Responsibilities

Individual-Giving Strategy & Donor Portfolio

Own the individual-giving strategy and pipeline.
Design and execute a multi-year plan for donor cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship — partnering with the CEO and Senior Director of Development to set cultivation stages and ensure every high-value donor has a clear next step.
Carry a personal portfolio.
Cultivate and steward individual and donor-advised-fund (DAF) donors with high-touch stewardship; standard acknowledgments are generated centrally.
Make leadership effective in donor moments.
Prepare the CEO and Senior Director of Development with briefing materials and deeper-engagement opportunities like site visits and program showcases.

Signature Events & Donor Experience

Own the Gala and signature events end-to-end.
Hold the strategy, budget, and execution — from concept through vendor and venue management and run-of-show, to post-event reconciliation and debrief, so each event outperforms the last.
Lead contracted and volunteer event capacity.
Direct a contracted event coordinator and volunteers, setting scope and holding accountability for execution.
Design a year-round engagement calendar
of cultivation moments — receptions, showcases, board touchpoints — between major events.

Giving Campaigns & Revenue Growth

Own campaign strategy and revenue.
Hold the strategy, segmentation, timeline, and revenue goals for Colorado Gives Day, End-of-Year Giving, and new campaigns you design — tracking performance in real time and adjusting tactics to meet or exceed targets.
Keep storytelling true.
Ensure campaign storytelling authentically reflects the youth, families, and communities CLF serves.

Coaching, Feedback & Growth

Report up with rigor.
Meet weekly with the Senior Director of Development to align priorities and surface risks; engage in quarterly coaching and an annual review.
Coach down to the capacity you lead.
Set clear scope and give growth-oriented feedback to the contracted event coordinator and volunteers.

Growth Path

This role begins as a non-supervisory builder position: the Director carries individual-giving strategy and relationships directly, supported by a contracted event coordinator and volunteers. As individual giving matures into a proven, dependable revenue stream, CLF expects to add development capacity reporting to this role.

Skills & Qualifications

Five to seven or more years of progressive development experience, with demonstrated ownership of donor cultivation, signature events, and giving campaigns, and a track record of growing individual or annual giving.
Demonstrated ability to set and meet revenue targets and to own budgets for events and campaigns.
Proficiency with donor management systems (Virtuous, Salesforce, Bloomerang, DonorPerfect, or similar); direct Virtuous experience preferred.
Excellent relationship and written-communication skills, with an ear for donor-facing language that is warm, specific, and anchored in mission.

About MyFriendBen
MyFriendBen is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit dedicated to making it easy for people to understand and access the government benefits, tax credits, and nonprofit programs they're eligible for. As MyFriendBen scales nationally, our donors and funders — foundations, corporations, government grantors, and individuals who believe in equitable access to the safety net — are essential partners in that growth, as is the internal team and culture that supports it.

Position Summary
The Director  of Operations is responsible for building and running the internal backbone of MyFriendBen — fundraising and grants, people operations, hiring and onboarding, team alignment, culture, and day-to-day organizational operations — so the organization can scale nationally without losing what makes it work. This role owns the systems, relationships, and practices that keep a fast-growing, distributed team funded, connected, effective, and aligned around MyFriendBen's mission.

The VP will manage a growing portfolio of fundraising and grant relationships — including grant writing, grant management, and donor stewardship — while also owning full-cycle hiring and onboarding, HR policies and practices, and team culture across a remote, multi-state staff. The role also oversees core operational functions, including finance and budget administration, vendor and systems management, and organizational planning, in partnership with the Executive Director.

This role works closely with the Executive Director, program, and leadership team, and reports regularly to the board of directors on fundraising results and organizational health. The ideal candidate brings progressive fundraising and operations experience, an entrepreneurial mindset, and genuine enthusiasm for MyFriendBen's mission of expanding access to public benefits.

Fundraising & Grants

About the Colorado LiftED Foundation

The Colorado LiftED Foundation is a long-term partner to youth and families in the Denver metro area, offering academic, social, and emotional support so no one has to navigate school and life alone. Since our founding in 1988, we've leveraged proven methods to give youth equal access to the resources they need to succeed — working toward a Colorado where every young person has equal access to educational and career opportunities that ignite their innate potential.

About the Position

The Director of Development & Engagement owns CLF's individual-giving engine — donor relationships, signature events, and year-round giving campaigns that turn community belief into sustained support for youth. Reporting to the Senior Director of Development, the Director sets and executes the strategy for donor cultivation and stewardship, the Annual Gala and signature events, and CLF's giving campaigns (Colorado Gives Day, End-of-Year Giving, and beyond), and owns the revenue those efforts produce.

This is a builder's role with a growth path: in year one it is non-supervisory, with the Director carrying strategy and donor relationships directly, supported by a contracted event coordinator and volunteers, and partnering closely with the CEO, Senior Director of Development, and Development Operations & Communications Manager. The ideal candidate is a strategic relationship-builder who is equally comfortable shaping a multi-year donor plan, running a flawless gala, and reading a campaign dashboard to course-correct mid-stream — someone who treats each donor as a long-term partner whose commitment is meant to outlast any single gift.

This Role Lives All Five CLF Values

A Seat at the Table —
Donor and volunteer experiences authentically include the voices of youth, families, and community.
An Inch Wide, A Mile Deep —
A focused, high-quality donor portfolio beats chasing volume.
Once a Dreamer, Always a Dreamer —
Every donor and volunteer is stewarded with the same long-term commitment CLF brings to youth.
Whatever It Takes —
Relentless, creative follow-through on cultivation, events, and campaigns alike.
We Not Me —
Individual giving is shared organizational infrastructure, not a department off to one side.

Key Responsibilities

Individual-Giving Strategy & Donor Portfolio

Own the individual-giving strategy and pipeline.
Design and execute a multi-year plan for donor cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship — partnering with the CEO and Senior Director of Development to set cultivation stages and ensure every high-value donor has a clear next step.
Carry a personal portfolio.
Cultivate and steward individual and donor-advised-fund (DAF) donors with high-touch stewardship; standard acknowledgments are generated centrally.
Make leadership effective in donor moments.
Prepare the CEO and Senior Director of Development with briefing materials and deeper-engagement opportunities like site visits and program showcases.

Signature Events & Donor Experience

Own the Gala and signature events end-to-end.
Hold the strategy, budget, and execution — from concept through vendor and venue management and run-of-show, to post-event reconciliation and debrief, so each event outperforms the last.
Lead contracted and volunteer event capacity.
Direct a contracted event coordinator and volunteers, setting scope and holding accountability for execution.
Design a year-round engagement calendar
of cultivation moments — receptions, showcases, board touchpoints — between major events.

Giving Campaigns & Revenue Growth

Own campaign strategy and revenue.
Hold the strategy, segmentation, timeline, and revenue goals for Colorado Gives Day, End-of-Year Giving, and new campaigns you design — tracking performance in real time and adjusting tactics to meet or exceed targets.
Keep storytelling true.
Ensure campaign storytelling authentically reflects the youth, families, and communities CLF serves.

Coaching, Feedback & Growth

Report up with rigor.
Meet weekly with the Senior Director of Development to align priorities and surface risks; engage in quarterly coaching and an annual review.
Coach down to the capacity you lead.
Set clear scope and give growth-oriented feedback to the contracted event coordinator and volunteers.

Growth Path

This role begins as a non-supervisory builder position: the Director carries individual-giving strategy and relationships directly, supported by a contracted event coordinator and volunteers. As individual giving matures into a proven, dependable revenue stream, CLF expects to add development capacity reporting to this role.

Skills & Qualifications

Five to seven or more years of progressive development experience, with demonstrated ownership of donor cultivation, signature events, and giving campaigns, and a track record of growing individual or annual giving.
Demonstrated ability to set and meet revenue targets and to own budgets for events and campaigns.
Proficiency with donor management systems (Virtuous, Salesforce, Bloomerang, DonorPerfect, or similar); direct Virtuous experience preferred.
Excellent relationship and written-communication skills, with an ear for donor-facing language that is warm, specific, and anchored in mission.
Experience directing contractors and/or volunteers, with the judgment to build and eventually supervise a small team.
Comfort with spreadsheets, email-marketing platforms, and reporting dashboards, and the analytical habit of using data to course-correct.
Deep commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion, belonging, and CLF's five core values.

Requirements

Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience in development, nonprofit management, communications, or a related field.
Availability for evening and weekend work tied to the Gala, cultivation events, and campaign deadlines.
Valid Colorado driver's license and reliable transportation for donor meetings and site visits.
Must pass a background check consistent with CLF's youth-serving organizational standards.
Alignment:
Demonstrated commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion, belonging, and CLF's core values (A Seat at the Table, We Not Me, An Inch Wide A Mile Deep, Once a Dreamer Always a Dreamer, Whatever It Takes).
